text.p: Uncertainty came back to haunt Italian debt markets as dealers sensed a sudden hesitancy in politicians' determination to address Italy's bloated budget deficit and carry out key reforms.
Analysts and brokers noted several factors combined to bump the March Btp future on LIFFE through a key support level at 130.80/85, opening the way to deeper losses than seen earlier.

But the hottest topic was how committed parts of the government now were to creating a 1997 mini-budget quickly or bringing forward the 1998 budget and cracking on with at least the first steps for vital pension reforms.

"Looking at Italian newspapers, the 1998 budget is looking unlikely to be anticipated before the summer and now there are doubts on 1997 mini budget. Apparently they are slowing down on this idea," one analyst at an Italian bank in London said.

"Add to this the feeling that the will to address pension reforms in a major way is somehow lacking. There's been a change in sentiment in the last two days. It's all under question and no longer certain," the analyst, who declined to be named said.
The March LIFFE future was 53 basis points off at 130.49 and the November 2006 Btp was 36 basis points off at 104.36. The spread over Germany tiptoed out to 169 from about 163 Wednesday.
Behind all this was the resurfacing concern that Italy's chances of meeting EMU criteria were once more slipping away.
Added to the political front, dealers said less interest than expected in 10 and 30 year government bond auctions also took its toll on the market.

Chartwise, while the March future remained in its uptrend, dealers noted volumes were tailing off as interest waned. Brokers said many investors lacked conviction over what direction they saw bond markets taking from here so were placing their money in other markets like currencies.
